maya: quick heads-up — observed reproducible token shift when serving int8-fused build on very long prompts (~30k tokens). starts fine but around token ~23900 generated sequence has an off-by-one token drift inside a code block :thinking:

kai: can you paste a tiny repro and confirm if float16 also shows it? :eyes:

maya: repro below. float16 looks clean. repro uses int8+fused-attn build running on local dev server.

```
# run locally (nn-serve)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-int8-fused","input":"<very long prompt>"}' > out.json
jq .out[23880:23920] out.json
```

luca: hmm that smells like a ring buffer wrap / pointer arithmetic bug in the sliding KV index. did you try different buffer_size?

maya: tried buffer=32768 and 65536, still repro. toggling prefetch_kv=false shifts the onset point by a few tokens but does not remove it. logs show attn_idx jumping backward by 1 at token 23988.

ci-bot: build 2026.03.18-int8-fuse completed (branch quant/fast-attn) — tests: 214 passed, 5 flaky (longctx smoke).

kai: paste the exact log lines and tell which RoPE variant (legacy/rescaled) the model uses.

maya: log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-18T14:22:19Z] INFO decoder: token=23986 attn_idx=23986
[2026-03-18T14:22:20Z] INFO decoder: token=23987 attn_idx=23987
[2026-03-18T14:22:21Z] INFO decoder: token=23988 attn_idx=23987  # <-- stuck one behind
[2026-03-18T14:22:21Z] WARN decoder: ringbuf_wrap delta=-1
```

luca: delta=-1 implies some int truncation or signed overflow in pointer math. any compile-time typedef changes between float and int8 kernels?

maya: our float build uses INDEX_T=int32 in kernels. int8 pipeline built with a smaller index typedef for memory footprint — looks like INDEX_T=int32 in host but a narrowed index in the fused-attn kernel IR. forcing INDEX_T=int64 locally eliminates the repro. perf drops ~4%.

kai: likely the IR emitter was casting a 64-bit offset down to 32-bit when lowering arithmetic for the fused kernel. check the code path that computes `pos = (base + offset)` then masks with `buffer_mask`. If mask calc expects 64-bit but result gets truncated, wrap semantics break for large offsets.

maya: confirmed: lowering pass inserts a truncating cast on `offset` when quant kernels are enabled. making the cast conditional on MAX_CTX or using saturating add for pointer arithmetic fixes it.

eva: we should avoid always switching to int64 globally. proposal: if MAX_CTX <= 1<<31 use int32 path, else promote to int64 for affected ops only. also add telemetry for attn_idx delta != 1.

luca: add a unit test that simulates very large offsets and both int8/float codegen paths. also add a quant-nightly longctx-smoke.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/4892 — includes guarded casts, repro script, logs, and a longctx-smoke CI job. tagging @oncall-ml for review.

ci-bot: PR 4892 opened by maya. CI: quant-nightly-longctx queued.

kai: can we add a micro-benchmark that measures the perf delta on the guarded int64 ops so SRE can decide backport tradeoffs?

maya: yes. local perf measurement shows ~4% throughput drop when we force int64 everywhere; guarded promotion is ~0.6% impact in our synthetic long-run. will include benchmark results in PR.

luca: any customer impact seen in logs?

maya: found one trace in SRE ticket RD-3421 with similar symptom (off-by-one in large generation). flagged CS and security. leaning to backport to 2026.02-stable with guarded change and telemetry.

eva: +1 for backport, add alert on metric `attn_ring_delta_non1_total` if rate > 1/hour/node.

maya: will add metric and alert; scheduling a 48h staging run with int8-fused and long prompts once CI green. thanks all :thumbsup:

kai: great catch and nice scoped fix.

eva: :rocket:
